key_insight: A commitment-based modification extends quantum position verification to a single-shot protocol that stays secure against entangled attackers even when photon loss is arbitrarily high.
engineering_relevance: This makes practical long-distance QPV more feasible for near-term quantum hardware by separating security from transmission loss while retaining implementable BB84-style primitives.
method: Adapt a BB84-based QPV protocol with a commitment threshold k for successfully received qubits.
Use no-signalling arguments to lift loss tolerance from sequential repetition to the parallel single-execution setting.
Prove adversarial success decays exponentially in k, preserving security against bounded-entanglement attacks.
evidence_signal: From the abstract, the protocol is proven secure under arbitrarily slow quantum communication and remains robust to noise levels up to 3.7%, with improved quantitative parameters from the refined analysis.
watch_item: The security guarantee depends on a chosen commitment threshold k and bounded-entanglement assumptions, so practical deployment must carefully validate device noise, timing, and implementation overhead.
paper_title: Arbitrarily Loss-Tolerant Quantum Position Verification in a Single Execution
